jobs.description: AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset. National Security customers are moving their most sensitive mission-critical workloads to AWS - and they need a technical advisor who understands both the technology and the stakes. As our Enterprise Support footprint grows across classified environments we're adding a Sr. Technical Account Manager (TAM) to meet that demand head-on. In this role you are the single most important technical relationship our National Security customers have at AWS. You'll sit at the intersection of cloud architecture, operational health, and customer strategy - working hands-on with customers as they adopt services like EC2, S3, DynamoDB, RDS, Lambda, SageMaker, ECS/EKS, GuardDuty, Systems Manager, OpenSearch, and Bedrock inside classified environments. You won't troubleshoot tickets directly but you will own the technical trajectory of your accounts: identifying risks before they become incidents driving architecture decisions that hold up under pressure and representing AWS in rooms where the margin for error is zero. This is not a sales role. It is a seat at the table with senior government and defense leaders who rely on your judgment to keep their operations running and evolving. This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph. Key job responsibilities • *Lead technical engagements** – Conduct deep-dive architecture reviews and operational health assessments to keep customer environments resilient and mission-ready. • *Design secure cloud solutions** – Partner with customers to architect and implement cloud-native systems that meet the unique security and compliance demands of classified workloads. • *Drive proactive risk management** – Identify operational gaps surface emerging risks and work with AWS service teams to resolve issues before they reach production. • *Accelerate adoption of AI/ML and autonomous capabilities** – Help customers integrate services like SageMaker, Bedrock, and ECS/EKS into their existing workflows translating cutting-edge technology into practical deployable solutions. • *Represent the customer inside AWS** – Advocate for your customers' technical needs across AWS service teams escalation paths and product roadmap discussions. A day in the life Most of your week is spent face-to-face (or screen-to-screen) with customers. Mondays typically start with cadence calls - checking in on open action items reviewing operational metrics and aligning on priorities for the week. Midweek is where the deeper work happens: leading Well-Architected reviews walking through architecture proposals or running incident post-mortems with customer engineering teams. When something breaks you're the one coordinating across AWS service teams to drive resolution and communicating status to senior leadership in real time. Between customer sessions you'll have focused time to research emerging AWS services relevant to your accounts prepare briefing materials and collaborate with fellow TAMs on patterns you're seeing across the national security space. Travel is approximately 10% or more as needed. This role will stretch you technically - every customer environment is different and the classified context adds layers of complexity that keep the work challenging. You'll build deep expertise in secure cloud architecture while developing the kind of executive-level advisory skills that define the next stage of your career. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses. We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. If you already have a Candidate Account, please Sign-In before you apply. Job Description: The Product Owner (PO) at Broadcom sits between the Product Manager (PM) and the Development Team. The PO's primary responsibility and value come from understanding and contributing towards the product strategy, and then executing that strategy by breaking down large strategic ideas and intentions into development items with concrete outcomes and then further into manageable work items—such as enablers or user stories—with the development team. The role requires a PO to navigate priorities across the mainframe software portfolio. Broadcom's Precision design system is a modern user interface framework, including both design assets and developer SDK, that delivers a consistent and intuitive user experience adopted by over 35 mainframe products in the Mainframe Software Portfolio. These distinct products are consumers of Precision assets, and by understanding all of the varied personas and use cases along with the value of the capability in the market, the PO is to prioritize features and capabilities across the development roadmap. Delivering user experiences that differentiate from the competition and are realized in the market within the solutions at the right time. This role requires negotiation across value streams and offering teams. The PO is the voice of the customer to the development and engineering processes, ensuring the right work is done at the right time to achieve the best outcomes for our customers—both external users and internal product teams who consume Precision assets. Product Owner Core Responsibilities Operates as part of an extended Product Management team, usually reporting to Product Management. Understands how the Enterprise backlog model operates with Epics, Capabilities, Features, and User Stories. Uses Program Increment (PI) Objectives and Iteration Goals to communicate with management. Establishes and sequences backlog items based on program priorities, events, and dependencies with other teams. Coordinates with other Product Owners, the System Team, and shared services in the Agile Release Train (ART) PI Planning meetings. Works with other Product Owners and the Product Management team throughout each Iteration and PI. The Product Owner owns the Definition of Done (DoD) and sets clear Acceptance Criteria, ultimately holding final authority to accept or reject completed user stories at the end of sprints. Team Backlog Ownership The principal responsibility of the PO is to maintain a backlog of work items with order and detail sufficient for the team to work on for the current and next iteration. A story must satisfy the team’s definition of ready. Cross-Team and Management Reporting To maintain cadence across many teams globally, PO communication is key to ensure inter-team dependencies are communicated and risks to team productivity are shared and mitigated. The PO is responsible for raising information to enable management by exception and is accountable for communication with their PO peers, PM's, engineering managers and Mainframe executives if needed. Customer Engagement Our business success is driven by our customers and in turn by their success. In order to ensure our products solve our customers' challenges we continually iterate on our solutions asking our customers for their feedback. A PO works with their PM and field peers, creating opportunities to visit customers and observe users in their environment whenever possible. Regular Sprint Reviews are one of the responsibilities of the PO who decides when it is appropriate to share progress and with which internal and external stakeholders. In establishing the Sprint Review event, the PO will invite their customers describing the value they may expect to receive. Typically performed over Zoom, a Sprint Review will showcase the most recent development. When a support case is escalated to the development team for further action, the PO must be aware of the case and may manage the case to completion. Collaboration with Product Manager(s), Engineering Manager(s) and Executives The Product Owner stands back to back with the Product Manager(s) and Engineering Managers(s), working together on the same broader problems but each tackling different areas of work and levels of detail. While the Product Manager(s) are considered ‘outward facing’ meeting potential customers and buyers, the Product Owner is considered ‘inward facing,’ focused on existing customers and colleagues in development and support. The Product Manager(s) answers the question “Why” do we choose to do this. This PO role will collaborate across many product managers and solution areas to negotiate business priorities and partners with cross value stream engineering leads and executives to secure the right priority and decision when this is needed.
